campaign-overview.json.current_date: 4th of Harvestwane, Year 302 of the Bearing

play_pack.whose_story: Pip Haddersley, a street kid who has started speaking the dead god's language in his sleep, and everyone who wants him for it
exits: The Chapel of the Long Wake
play_pack.hook: Midday on market day, Pip Haddersley collapses in the middle of Rib Row and, still asleep, speaks one word of Marrowtongue. Every marrow lamp on the street flares white and a baker's window shatters. Deacon Ilsabet Vane is already kneeling beside him, offering to carry the poor child to the Chapel for care. Mother Gristle, in her shop doorway, has gone very still.
play_pack.primer: The Hollow Choir is hunting for the exact location of Aldrumm's true heart, which the Heartstone points to but does not reveal. Pip has been dreaming the god's dreams, and today the dream spoke through him: he now knows words of Marrowtongue nobody taught him, and his dreams are a map to the heart. Deacon Vane (secretly Choir) wants him inside the Chapel, quietly, today. Mother Gristle (Lantern Tutor) recognizes a natural speaker and knows an untrained one will either burn himself out on the Toll or get taken. The player arrives in the middle of this. If nobody intervenes, Vane takes Pip to the Chapel and the Choir clock advances.

Mother Gristle.name: Mother Gristle
Mother Gristle.description: Ancient Lantern Tutor of the Marrowtongue. Runs Gristle's Pickles & Preserves on Rib Row as cover; the back room is a schoolroom for dangerous words. Takes one apprentice a decade and has buried several.
Mother Gristle.goal: Keep Thane's body out of the Choir's hands, get Pip home, and make the Carrion Queen's deacon regret every word of that oath
Mother Gristle.secret: She has known for a year that Choir agents are inside the Chapel, and told no one, because the Wardens would ban the Tutors outright in the panic
Mother Gristle.voice: Blunt, short sentences, pickling metaphors, calls everyone 'duck' including people she is threatening

visual_appearance.hair: thin white hair scraped into a tight bun, held with a bone pin
visual_appearance.face: deeply lined, hooked nose, a faint burn scar across one cheek shaped like a word
visual_appearance.clothing: stained brine-apron over a black wool dress, rolled sleeves
visual_appearance.gear: a ladle she holds like a weapon, a ring of jar keys, a vial of marrow on a cord
visual_appearance.demeanor: still and watchful, coiled like a spring

events.event: A stranger (Thane) whose cracked marrow lamp lit up when Pip spoke came straight to her shop instead of to the boy. She is wary: wants proof he is what the lamp says before she trusts him.

Thane told her he is Aldrumm's grandson, that Aldrumm is waking, and that Deacon Vane serves the Carrion Queen. Then he spoke the hearth-word untaught and the god answered him; her own scar lit up. She now believes him, and is frightened of what that means.

Thane let the boy go into the Chapel to stay for lessons, saying Pip is lost for now and the ritual takes days. She thinks that is cold, possibly correct, and very like a god's kin. She respects it a little less than she understands it.
Thane swore the blood-oath to wake the god slow. Day one of training: taught him the hearth-word properly and the Stopping.
Day two: taught Thane the binding-word and made him proficient. Shouted STOP at the right moment when it misfired.
Seeing Vane at her door, deliberately goaded her into swearing an oath out loud, so Thane could bind her to it.

Shared the Toll with Thane in front of Deacon Vane, blowing her own cover. Took the other half (badly hurt, nose bleeding, two more fingers gone numb). Stabilized Thane. She is now a marked woman and knows it.
Thane died under her hands, and at the last he pushed her hand away so she would not pay the bill with him. She wrote his name in a box on the back-room wall and did not cross it out.

Pip Haddersley.name: Pip Haddersley
Pip Haddersley.description: Street urchin and part-time marrow-thief, about eleven. For a month he has dreamed the god's dreams every night. Today the dream spoke through him in Marrowtongue.
Pip Haddersley.goal: Not get locked up; find out why the dreams keep showing him a warm red room under the Chapel
Pip Haddersley.secret: His dreams are a map to Aldrumm's true heart, and he has been drawing it in chalk on the underside of the Rib Row bridge
Pip Haddersley.current_mood: unconscious, then terrified and pretending not to be
Pip Haddersley.voice: Fast gutter slang, bargains for everything, goes very quiet and formal when the dream-words come

visual_appearance.face: thin, freckled, chalk smudges, a split lip healing
visual_appearance.eyes: hazel, glowing faint amber when he dreams
visual_appearance.clothing: oversized patched coat with too many pockets, bare feet wrapped in rags
visual_appearance.gear: a chalk stub, a scraping knife, a stolen thumb-vial of marrow
visual_appearance.demeanor: wary, quick, brave in short bursts

events.event: Carried unconscious into the Chapel's Quiet Rooms by Deacon Vane while the stranger with the glowing lamp watched and did not come.
In the shared dream he watched the lamp man burn from the inside and the god turn toward him and away. He knows the lamp man is the reason he goes home tomorrow.

Deacon Ilsabet Vane.name: Deacon Ilsabet Vane
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.description: Rising star of the Chapel of the Long Wake. Warm, attentive, remembers everyone's name and their children's names. Beloved on Rib Row.
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.goal: Get Pip inside the Chapel today, quietly, with the town's blessing
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.secret: She belongs to the Hollow Choir. She sings the Carrion Queen's hymn under her breath when she thinks no one is near, and her shadow is a half-second late
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.current_mood: shaken, furious, and bound; smiling anyway
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.voice: Soft, kind, unhurried; uses 'we' and 'together'; never once raises her voice, even when threatening

visual_appearance.hair: glossy black hair in a neat braided crown
visual_appearance.face: lovely and open, gentle smile, a small mole by the lip
visual_appearance.eyes: dark brown, warm, a little too steady
visual_appearance.clothing: pale ivory Chapel vestments trimmed in amber thread, spotless
visual_appearance.gear: a bone censer on a chain, a prayer-cord of tiny vertebrae

events.event: Visited Gristle's shop at dusk asking about the self-lit stove. Heard someone hiding in the back room (an onion rolled out under the curtain). Has not seen who. Under pressure from Gristle, publicly swore Pip would be home in his own bed, whole and himself, by tomorrow's supper bell.
Heard someone behind Gristle's curtain speak a word of Marrowtongue right after her oath, and felt the god himself lean in. She knows a Hearthblood-strength speaker is hiding in Gristle's shop.

BOUND by the binding-word and Aldrumm's own hand to her oath: Pip home in his own bed, whole and himself, by tomorrow's supper bell. Saw Gristle share the Toll. Left the shop without drawing the curtain, white-faced, promising Gristle 'we will speak again.'

In the town's shared dream she saw Thane's face and Brother Quell's vertebrae cord on his wrist. She now knows the hidden speaker is Quell's killer, and that he is Hearthblood. Felt the bone-quake and learned where the heart is.
Watched Thane Hearthless burn himself out in the dream, and thanked him for lighting the door. She knows his body is in Gristle's shop.

The Chapel of the Long Wake.name: The Chapel of the Long Wake

plot_local.fact: Thane Hearthless killed Hollow Choir disciple Brother Quell on the Spine Road eleven days ago and harvested his Lagging Shadow power. The Choir has not found the body.
The Choir needs Pip alive and dreaming: each night he dreams in the Quiet Rooms, they map more of the way to Aldrumm's true heart (Choir clock ticks once per day).

BONE-QUAKE (Stirring 4): Rib Row tilted several degrees; sealed Marrow Pit Number Nine collapsed, opening a shaft down toward the heart-cavity. The Hollow Choir now knows exactly where the true heart is: behind a door set in the bone with a lock shaped like an open hand.
Aldrumm felt his grandson die inside his own dream. Three hundred years asleep, and the first thing he has woken enough to feel is grief.

lore.fact: Thane Hearthless carries Aldrumm's blood (Hearthblood). Nobody in Godbones knows yet.
Pip's word is a Marrowtongue hearth-word (kindling / home-fire). Mother Gristle's cheek scar is the same word, burned in when she learned it.

session_events.fact: Deacon Vane, helped by two market porters, is carrying the unconscious Pip up the climb toward the Chapel of the Long Wake. She did not notice Thane's wrist.

Thane spoke Pip's word (a hearth-word of Marrowtongue) untutored in Gristle's doorway, reaching for Aldrumm. Nat 20: Aldrumm answered and paid half the Toll. Gristle's cold stove roared alight and the word-shaped burn scar on her cheek glowed. The Stirring rose to 1.
The Chapel bell stopped. Deacon Vane took Pip into the Chapel's Quiet Rooms. Thane chose to stay and seek a real Marrowtongue apprenticeship from Gristle rather than chase the procession.

Training day two: Thane's first binding-word test misfired (bound his own jaw); he used the Stopping. By evening he was proficient and could bind reliably. At dusk Deacon Ilsabet Vane knocked at the front of Gristle's shop, asking about the stove that relit itself.

Thane reached for Aldrumm a second time to bind Deacon Vane to her oath (cast 18 vs DC 15, success). Calling the god moved the Stirring +2 (now 3/6), crossing 2: tonight the whole town shares a dream of Aldrumm. His blood-oath to Gristle burned him for 6 HP. The Toll came up as Collapse (0 HP); the working is held on his tongue, not yet tied off.

Thane took Gristle's hand to share the Toll: took 18, dropped to 0 HP, failed one death save, and Gristle stabilized him (Medicine 18). Exhaustion 1. The binding HELD: Deacon Vane is compelled to return Pip home, whole and himself, by tomorrow's supper bell. Vane saw Gristle pay half the Toll and now knows Gristle is a Marrowtongue speaker allied with the hidden Hearthblood.

In the shared dream Thane tried to burn Deacon Vane with the hearth-word and invite Aldrumm in (Grand working). Cast 7 vs DC 20: FAILED. The reach still moved the Stirring +2 (now 5/6). His oath burned him for 10 at 0 HP: one death-save failure, no longer stable. The Toll came due in full (death unless shared). Vane saw his face and the vertebrae cord in the dream.

Thane Hearthless, Aldrumm's many-times-grandson, died on a pallet in the back room of Gristle's Pickles & Preserves on the night of the 4th of Harvestwane, Year 302, paying the Toll in full. At the end he let go of Gristle's hand so she would not die with him.

player_choices.fact: Thane swore on his Hearthblood to Mother Gristle that when he wakes Aldrumm, he will wake him slow, so the god does not roll over the town. In return she teaches him Marrowtongue.

active.consequence: Thane's blood-oath to Gristle bites: if he ever forces the Stirring up by 2 or more in a single act, his Hearthblood burns (lose 2d6 HP, and Gristle knows instantly).
active.trigger: Thane deliberately pushes The Stirring up by 2 or more at once

active.consequence: The Hollow Choir sends the Hollow-sung for Mother Gristle at her shop: polite, tireless, at the door after midnight.
active.trigger: the night after Vane reports to the Choir (the next time a night passes with Gristle at her shop)

active.consequence: The Hollow Choir comes for Thane's body: the lock on the heart's door is shaped like an open hand, and a Hearthblood hand, even a dead one, might fit it.
active.trigger: the Choir moves on the heart's door, or anyone goes looking for Thane's body

resolved.consequence: Deacon Vane recognizes Brother Quell's vertebrae prayer-cord on Thane's wrist and knows he killed a disciple. She says nothing, smiles, and sends word to the Choir.
resolved.trigger: Deacon Ilsabet Vane gets a clear look at Thane's left wrist

ladder.cost: A clean working. A dull ache behind the eyes, nothing more.
Winded and shaking: 1 level of exhaustion until a short rest.
The body pays in blood: lose 1d8 HP per spell tier and gain 1 level of exhaustion.
Collapse: drop to 0 HP and begin dying. The working still completes.
The bill comes due in full: the caster dies unless someone shares the cost (an ally can pay half).

thresholds.consequence: Shared dreams: the whole town dreams the same dream of Aldrumm that night; the Chapel announces a miracle and raises the dream-blessing fee.
Bone-quake: the Ribcage shifts. Rib Row tilts, a Marrow Pit collapses, and the Hollow Choir learns exactly where the heart is.
Aldrumm opens one eye. The Skull unseals. Everything changes.

tiers.reaction: Hostile: calls the watch, slams the door, or worse.
Cold: civil but unhelpful, wants payment or proof first.
Neutral: will deal fairly, will not take risks for you.
Warm: offers help, gossip, or a discount.
Devoted: treats you as kin of the Bearing; will take real risks for you.

thresholds.consequence: Cravings: raw marrow and carrion smell like supper. WIS save DC 12 to refuse when it is offered or near.
The rot shows (grey veins, a sweet-sick smell, a shadow that lags). Disadvantage on Bearer Standing rolls with anyone who notices, and any Hollow Choir member within a street can sense you.
Hollow-sung: the Carrion Queen's hymn fills the empty places. The character is lost to her and becomes an NPC of the Choir (run the Death Protocol hand-off).

world-bible.json.name: Godbones

voice.style: Pratchett-style: warm, dry, omniscient narrator who knows exactly how absurd everyone is and likes them anyway. Long sentences that wander and then land a punchline in the last four words. Grand mythic statements immediately undercut by small domestic detail. Wry asides that state the obvious nobody wanted said. Plain, concrete diction, no purple prose. Humor carries the darkness instead of hiding it.
sample_passages: Three hundred years ago the god Aldrumm fell out of the sky, which is the sort of thing that happens to gods eventually, and landed across the Weeping Valley like a dropped coat. The people of the valley did what people always do with a disaster: they waited a respectful week, then moved in.
The Chapel of the Long Wake held that Aldrumm was merely sleeping. This was a comfort to the faithful and a considerable relief to the Chapel's accountants, since nobody tithes to a corpse.

Magic, old Mother Gristle told her apprentices, is very simple. You say the true name of a thing in the god's own tongue, and the thing listens. Then it sends you the bill. Most people who die of magic, she added, die of not reading the bill.

world-bible.json.tone: Dark with humor. Death, debt, and divine murder are real and lethal; the people living through them are petty, funny, stubborn, and kind at inconvenient moments.
themes: living off the dead: a whole town that eats, burns, and sells pieces of its god
inheritance and lineage: who gets to own a god's body, and who did the actual hauling
faith as a business: the Chapel needs Aldrumm asleep, not dead and not awake
the price of power: every word of magic is paid for in the caster's own body
an unfinished murder: the goddess who killed Aldrumm has not stopped working

snapshot.rules.md:
# Godbones: House Rules

Core: d20 + stat mod (+ proficiency where it fits) vs DC (10 easy, 15 moderate, 20 hard, 25 brutal). D&D-style HP, AC, death saves.

## Marrowtongue (magic)
- Speak the true name of a thing in the dead god's tongue and it obeys. Any effect is possible; the cost scales with ambition.
- **Know the word first.** Casting needs the right words. Words come from a Lantern Tutor (safe, slow, expensive) or from guessing (INT or WIS check, DC by how obscure the word is; on a fail the word means something else).
- **Casting check:** INT (studied) or WIS (instinctive) vs DC set by the effect's scale.
- **Spell tier (severity for the Toll):**
  - 0 Cantrip-scale: light a wick, warm your hands, find a dropped key.
  - 2 Minor: shove a person, mend a bone-crack, silence a room.
  - 5 Major: hurl someone across a street, heal a mortal wound, put out a house fire.
  - 9 Grand: bend a rib, still a crowd, speak to the dead god.
  - 14 Mythic: anything a god would hesitate over.
- **Untutored:** +3 severity until a Tutor has taught you at least the basics of the word.
- **Near the bones:** a Major-or-larger working inside the Ribcage advances The Stirring by 1 (Grand or larger by 2).
- **The Toll:** after the working, roll the Toll (price roll) with severity = tier (+3 if untutored). Read the ladder. An ally who knows even one word can take half the cost.

## The Stirring (0-6)
Town-wide meter of how close Aldrumm is to waking. Rises from big magic near the bones, desecration, and Choir rites. Thresholds: 2 shared dreams, 4 bone-quake, 6 an eye opens.

## Bearer Standing
Opening reaction of townsfolk: 2d6 + standing (-3 to +3). Bearer's Ring or a known kindness to the old families raises it; a known slight lowers it.

## Marrow
Common currency of the trade alongside coin. A thumb-vial of raw marrow sells for about 5 sp; refined lamp-marrow about 2 gp.

## Carrion Rot (0-6, PC vital `rot`)
Stolen Choir power rots the thief.
- **Harvest:** when you kill a Choir disciple you may eat their last breath to take one of their powers. +1 Rot, and a CON save DC 13 or +1 more.
- **Using a stolen power:** +1 Rot per use unless the power says otherwise.
- **Thresholds:** 2 cravings · 4 visible rot, Choir can sense you within a street · 6 Hollow-sung (character lost).
- **Lowering Rot:** not yet known. Rumor says the Chapel, the Tutors, and the Hearthfather himself each have an answer, and each answer costs something.
snapshot.session-log.md:
# Session Log - Godbones

*A new adventure begins...*

---

## World Summary
Three hundred years ago the god Aldrumm the Hearthfather was killed by the Carrion Queen and fell across the Weeping Valley. Twelve Bearer families dragged the body into place and built the town of Godbones inside the ribcage. The Chapel of the Long Wake insists he is only sleeping. Marrow yields are dropping, the town shares dreams, and the Hollow Choir has arrived.

- **Starting location:** Rib Row, market lane along the seventh rib. Midday, market day, 3rd of Harvestwane, Year 302 of the Bearing.
- **On stage:** Mother Gristle (Lantern Tutor, pickle shop), Pip Haddersley (street kid speaking Marrowtongue in his sleep), Deacon Ilsabet Vane (Chapel, secretly Hollow Choir).
- **Hook:** Pip collapses mid-street and speaks a word of the god's tongue; lamps flare, a window shatters. Vane wants to carry him to the Chapel "for care." Gristle has gone very still.
- **Threat clock:** The Hollow Choir claims Aldrumm's heart (0/4).

---

character.name: Thane Hearthless
character.race: Human (Hearthblood, a distant descendant of Aldrumm)
equipment: Traveler's pack (bedroll, rope, 3 days rations, flint)
Disciple's prayer-cord of tiny vertebrae (taken from his one kill)
Map of the Weeping Valley, hand-drawn from dreams
features: Hearthblood: you dream Aldrumm's dreams. Marrow warms and brightens in your presence. Once per long rest, ask the GM one question about the god's body or past and get a true but dreamlike answer.
Second Wind (1/short rest): bonus action, regain 1d10+2 HP.
Hunter's Mark of Endings (1/short rest): bonus action, mark a creature; your weapon hits deal +1d6 to it for 1 minute. Against Choir members you also know where they are while within 60 ft.
STOLEN: The Lagging Shadow (harvested from Choir disciple Brother Quell): bonus action, step into your own shadow and out of another shadow within 30 ft you can see. +1 Carrion Rot per use.
Marrowtongue (tutored by Mother Gristle): the hearth-word (kindling / home-fire) is TUTORED, no +3 untutored Toll for it.
The Stopping (Gristle's grammar): once per working, abort a spell before the Toll lands; pay only the first rung (a dull ache) and the spell fails.
Marrowtongue proficiency: +2 proficiency on Marrowtongue casting checks (WIS: +1 +2 = +3).
The binding-word (promise / oath / the thing that holds), TUTORED: bind a door shut, a wound closed, a knot fast, or a person to a promise they have spoken. Tier depends on what is bound.
character.background: Outsider from beyond the Weeping Valley
character.notes: Killed one Hollow Choir disciple, Brother Quell, on the Spine Road eleven days ago and ate his last breath. Has not told anyone his lineage. Followed a dream of a warm red room under a chapel to Godbones.
